[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''Robert Glasgow''' was baptised or born at Glencorse on 29 December 1676, a son of [[Glasgow-3012|John Glasgow]] and [[Currie-4998|Margaret Currie]].<ref name="Robert1676">Scotland's People, Church of Scotland old parish registers, Robert Glasgow, 29 December 1676, parents John Glasgow and Margaret Currie, Glencorse parish 687, reference 10/8.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-3012]] is assessed at 88% (probable). Robert’s 1676 Glencorse baptism names John Glasgow and Margaret Currie. Their 1673 Kirknewton marriage supplies an earlier named couple in the neighbouring district, favouring the existing John household over an otherwise unspecified namesake.

Complete profile placement88%; the 1649 child-to-adult John identification remains inferred. The 1704 Robert/Davidson marriage is a different event.

Next useful test: Compare the 1673 and 1676 entries for residence and witnesses.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-3011 Scotland's People, Church of Scotland old parish registers, Robert Glasgow, 29 December 1676, parents John Glasgow and Margaret Currie, Glencorse parish 687, reference 10/8.]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.



An exact Scotland's People search for Robert Glasgow baptisms at Glencorse from 1640 through 1690 returns only this entry. A Robert Glasgow married [[Davidson-20783|Margaret Davidson]] in the same parish on 8 June 1704, when this Robert would have been twenty-seven.<ref name="Marriage1704">Scotland's People, Church of Scotland old parish registers, marriage of Robert Glasgow and Margarett Davidson, 8 June 1704, Glencorse parish 687, reference 20/53.</ref> The unique indexed local candidate, matching parish and chronology, makes this Robert a strong candidate for that groom and the couple's children. The marriage index gives no age, parents or occupation, so the identity remains unproved and no spouse or children are attached here yet.

An exact Scotland's People wills-and-testaments search for Robert Glasgow from 1690 through 1760, repeated under Glasgo, Glascow, Glaskow and Glassgow, returned no result. Targeted inspection of the Glencorse kirk-session testimonial register found no Robert Glasgow or Margaret Davidson on the pages covering 1704, 1708, 1710 and 1720.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Glencorse kirk session, CH2/181/1, testimonials (1685–1728), targeted pages for 1704, 1708, 1710 and 1720, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/virtual-volumes/volume-images/volume_data-CH2-181-1/REX00185 Scotland's People Virtual Volumes].</ref> These are limited negatives: neither source is a population list, and spelling variation or register gaps may conceal relevant evidence.

This Robert was seventeen in October 1694 and is also chronologically capable of being the Robt Glasgow then listed as a servant in Alexander Ainslie's North Leith glass-manufactory household.<ref>National Records of Scotland, E70/4/10, North Leith poll tax, 3 October 1694, image 11, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/virtual-volumes/volume-images/volume_data-E70-4-10/REX01666?image_number=11 Scotland's People Virtual Volumes].</ref> On 16 July 1694 a Robert Glasgow gave a receipt in Ainslie's name for bottles supplied to the Earl of Breadalbane.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Breadalbane Muniments, GD112/15/59, item 24, 16 July 1694, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD112%2F15%2F59 catalogue description].</ref> The shared employer and year make him almost certainly the October servant and prove a functional glassworks-business role, but neither record identifies him with the Glencorse child.

Neither possible continuation identifies this man as [[Glasgow-2867|Robert Glasgow]], master of the ''John and Archibald'' in 1754.
